question: Which country is the host of the 2023 ODI Cricket World Cup event?
solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India is hosting the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 for the fourth time. The previous years were 1987, 1996, and 2011.
 
• This will be the 13th edition of the Men's Cricket World Cup, organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• The tournament is expected to feature 10 teams from around the world, competing over several weeks for the prestigious trophy.
 
• India has previously won the Cricket World Cup twice, in 1983 under the captaincy of Kapil Dev and in 2011 under the captaincy of MS Dhoni.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC (International Cricket Council)**

 
 
• The ICC is the global governing body for cricket, responsible for the organization and governance of cricket's major international tournaments.
 
• It was founded as the Imperial Cricket Conference in 1909 by representatives from England, Australia, and South Africa.
 
• The ICC has 104 member countries, including 12 full members that play Test matches and 92 associate members.
 
 
 
• **Cricket World Cup**
 
 
• The Cricket World Cup is an international championship of One Day International (ODI) cricket.
 
• The event is organized by the sport's governing body, the ICC, every four years.
 
• The first Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975, and since then, it has grown to become one of the most watched sporting events globally.
 
• The tournament format has evolved over the years, with the current format featuring a round-robin group stage followed by knockout rounds.
 
 
 
• **One Day International (ODI)**
 
 
• An ODI is a form of limited-overs cricket, played between two teams with international status.
 
• Each team faces a set number of overs, usually 50, and the team that scores the most runs wins the match.
 
• ODIs are recognized for their exciting and fast-paced nature, as compared to Test matches, which can last up to five days.
